title: The Impact of Education on Chronic Disease Risk

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy

**Method: Instrumental Variables (IV / Two-Stage Least Squares)**

**Rationale:** The relationship between education (`x`) and chronic disease (`y`) is likely endogenous — unobserved factors (e.g., innate ability, family background, health consciousness) simultaneously affect both education and health outcomes. OLS estimates would be biased and inconsistent.

**Instrument:** Quarter-of-birth (`z`) is used as an instrument for years of education, following the classic Angrist & Krueger (1991) logic. Compulsory schooling laws interact with quarter-of-birth to create exogenous variation in educational attainment — individuals born in certain quarters are compelled to complete more schooling before they can legally drop out.

**Key Assumptions:**
1. **Relevance:** Quarter-of-birth is correlated with years of education (testable via first-stage F-statistic).
2. **Exclusion Restriction:** Quarter-of-birth affects chronic disease *only* through its effect on education, not through any direct channel (untestable but standard in this literature).
3. **Independence:** Quarter-of-birth is as-good-as-randomly assigned (plausible given biological determination).

## 2. R Code

```r
# ============================================================
# IV Analysis: Impact of Education on Chronic Disease Risk
# ============================================================

# Load required packages
if (!require("AER")) install.packages("AER", repos="https://cran.r-project.org")
if (!require("lmtest")) install.packages("lmtest", repos="https://cran.r-project.org")
if (!require("sandwich")) install.packages("sandwich", repos="https://cran.r-project.org")

library(AER)
library(lmtest)
library(sandwich)

# --------------------------------------------------
# 1. Load and inspect data
# --------------------------------------------------
df <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s72_data.csv")

cat("=== Data Summary ===\n")
cat("Observations:", nrow(df), "\n")
cat("Variables:", ncol(df), "\n\n")
summary(df)

cat("\n=== Correlation Matrix ===\n")
print(round(cor(df), 4))

# --------------------------------------------------
# 2. OLS Estimation (Naive / Benchmark)
# --------------------------------------------------
cat("\n\n========================================\n")
cat("OLS ESTIMATION (Potentially Biased)\n")
cat("========================================\n")

ols_no_controls <- lm(y ~ x, data = df)
ols_with_controls <- lm(y ~ x + controls, data = df)

cat("\n--- OLS without controls ---\n")
print(summary(ols_no_controls))

cat("\n--- OLS with controls ---\n")
print(summary(ols_with_controls))

# Robust standard errors for OLS
cat("\n--- OLS with robust SE (with controls) ---\n")
print(coeftest(ols_with_controls, vcov = vcovHC(ols_with_controls, type = "HC1")))

# --------------------------------------------------
# 3. First Stage: z -> x
# --------------------------------------------------
cat("\n\n========================================\n")
cat("FIRST STAGE: z -> x\n")
cat("========================================\n")

first_stage <- lm(x ~ z + controls, data = df)
print(summary(first_stage))

# First-stage F-statistic for instrument relevance
first_stage_restricted <- lm(x ~ controls, data = df)
f_test <- anova(first_stage_restricted, first_stage)
cat("\n--- First-Stage F-test for instrument relevance ---\n")
print(f_test)

f_stat <- summary(first_stage)$fstatistic
cat("\nFirst-stage F-statistic on z (from full regression F):", 
    round(f_stat[1], 2), "\n")

# Partial F-stat specifically for the instrument
# (coefficient on z / SE)^2
z_coef <- coef(first_stage)["z"]
z_se <- summary(first_stage)$coefficients["z", "Std. Error"]
partial_f <- (z_coef / z_se)^2
cat("Partial F-statistic for z:", round(partial_f, 2), "\n")
cat("Rule of thumb: F > 10 indicates strong instrument\n")

if (partial_f < 10) {
  cat("WARNING: Weak instrument concern (F < 10)!\n")
} else {
  cat("Instrument passes weak instrument test.\n")
}

# --------------------------------------------------
# 4. IV / 2SLS Estimation
# --------------------------------------------------
cat("\n\n========================================\n")
cat("IV / 2SLS ESTIMATION\n")
cat("========================================\n")

# IV without controls
iv_no_controls <- ivreg(y ~ x | z, data = df)
cat("\n--- IV without controls ---\n")
print(summary(iv_no_controls, diagnostics = TRUE))

# IV with controls
iv_with_controls <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls | z + controls, data = df)
cat("\n--- IV with controls ---\n")
print(summary(iv_with_controls, diagnostics = TRUE))

# Robust standard errors for IV
cat("\n--- IV with robust SE (with controls) ---\n")
robust_iv <- coeftest(iv_with_controls, vcov = vcovHC(iv_with_controls, type = "HC1"))
print(robust_iv)

# --------------------------------------------------
# 5. Manual 2SLS (verification)
# --------------------------------------------------
cat("\n\n========================================\n")
cat("MANUAL 2SLS VERIFICATION\n")
cat("========================================\n")

# Stage 1: predict x from z and controls
stage1 <- lm(x ~ z + controls, data = df)
df$x_hat <- fitted(stage1)

# Stage 2: regress y on predicted x and controls
stage2 <- lm(y ~ x_hat + controls, data = df)
cat("Manual 2SLS coefficient on education:", round(coef(stage2)["x_hat"], 4), "\n")
cat("AER ivreg coefficient on education:", round(coef(iv_with_controls)["x"], 4), "\n")

# --------------------------------------------------
# 6. Reduced Form: z -> y
# --------------------------------------------------
cat("\n\n========================================\n")
cat("REDUCED FORM: z -> y\n")
cat("========================================\n")

reduced_form <- lm(y ~ z + controls, data = df)
print(summary(reduced_form))

# Wald estimator
rf_coef <- coef(reduced_form)["z"]
fs_coef <- coef(first_stage)["z"]
wald <- rf_coef / fs_coef
cat("Wald (IV) estimate =", round(wald, 4), "\n")
cat("This should match the 2SLS estimate.\n")

# --------------------------------------------------
# 7. Robustness Checks
# --------------------------------------------------
cat("\n\n========================================\n")
cat("ROBUSTNESS CHECKS\n")
cat("========================================\n")

# Check 1: Balance test - instrument should not predict controls
cat("\n--- Balance Test: Does z predict controls? ---\n")
balance_test <- lm(controls ~ z, data = df)
print(summary(balance_test))
cat("p-value for z:", round(summary(balance_test)$coefficients["z", "Pr(>|t|)"], 4), "\n")
cat("(High p-value = good: instrument is as-good-as-random)\n")

# Check 2: Hausman test (endogeneity test)
cat("\n--- Hausman Endogeneity Test ---\n")
# Add first-stage residuals to OLS
df$fs_resid <- residuals(first_stage)
hausman_reg <- lm(y ~ x + controls + fs_resid, data = df)
hausman_p <- summary(hausman_reg)$coefficients["fs_resid", "Pr(>|t|)"]
cat("p-value on first-stage residuals:", round(hausman_p, 4), "\n")
if (hausman_p < 0.05) {
  cat("REJECT exogeneity: IV is preferred over OLS\n")
} else {
  cat("FAIL TO REJECT exogeneity: OLS may be consistent\n")
}

# Check 3: Compare OLS vs IV
cat("\n\n--- Summary Comparison ---\n")
cat("OLS estimate (with controls):", round(coef(ols_with_controls)["x"], 4), "\n")
cat("IV estimate (with controls):", round(coef(iv_with_controls)["x"], 4), "\n")
cat("Difference (IV - OLS):", 
    round(coef(iv_with_controls)["x"] - coef(ols_with_controls)["x"], 4), "\n")

# Check 4: Anderson-Rubin confidence interval (robust to weak instruments)
cat("\n--- Anderson-Rubin Weak-Instrument Robust Inference ---\n")
# Grid search for AR test
beta_grid <- seq(coef(iv_with_controls)["x"] - 3, 
                  coef(iv_with_controls)["x"] + 3, length.out = 1000)
ar_pvals <- sapply(beta_grid, function(b) {
  y_tilde <- df$y - b * df$x
  ar_reg <- lm(y_tilde ~ z + controls, data = df)
  coef(summary(ar_reg))["z", "Pr(>|t|)"]
})
ar_ci <- range(beta_grid[ar_pvals > 0.05])
cat("Anderson-Rubin 95% CI:", round(ar_ci[1], 4), "to", round(ar_ci[2], 4), "\n")

# --------------------------------------------------
# 8. Final Summary
# --------------------------------------------------
cat("\n\n========================================\n")
cat("FINAL RESULTS SUMMARY\n")
cat("========================================\n")
cat("Research Question: Does education reduce chronic disease risk?\n\n")
cat(sprintf("OLS Coefficient on Education:  %.4f (SE: %.4f)\n", 
            coef(ols_with_controls)["x"],
            summary(ols_with_controls)$coefficients["x", "Std. Error"]))
cat(sprintf("IV Coefficient on Education:   %.4f (SE: %.4f)\n",
            coef(iv_with_controls)["x"],
            summary(iv_with_controls)$coefficients["x", "Std. Error"]))
cat(sprintf("First-Stage Partial F:         %.2f\n", partial_f))
cat(sprintf("Hausman Test p-value:          %.4f\n", hausman_p))
cat(sprintf("Reduced Form (z -> y):         %.4f\n", rf_coef))
cat(sprintf("First Stage (z -> x):          %.4f\n", fs_coef))
```

## 3. Expected Findings

**Expected sign and magnitude:**

1. **OLS estimate:** Likely negative — more education is associated with lower chronic disease incidence. However, this estimate is potentially biased (direction of bias is ambiguous; omitted variables like innate health consciousness could bias OLS toward finding a stronger protective effect).

2. **IV estimate:** Expected to be **negative**, indicating that an additional year of education causally reduces chronic disease risk. The IV estimate may differ from OLS in magnitude:
   - If OLS is biased toward zero (due to measurement error in education), IV will be *more* negative.
   - If OLS is biased away from zero (due to omitted variables correlated with both education and health), IV will be *less* negative.

3. **First-stage F-statistic:** Quarter-of-birth is a historically weak instrument (Angrist & Krueger's original application had very large samples). With only 500 observations, there is a real concern that the partial F may be **below 10**, raising weak instrument issues. If so, the IV estimates will have wide confidence intervals and may be unreliable.

4. **Magnitude:** Given the continuous outcome variable and the data scale observed in the preview, the IV coefficient likely falls in the range of **-0.5 to -1.5** (a one-year increase in education reduces the chronic disease index by 0.5–1.5 units), though this depends heavily on the data-generating process and instrument strength.

5. **Reduced form:** The direct effect of quarter-of-birth on chronic disease (`z → y`) should be small but negative if the causal chain operates through education.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Quarter-of-birth serves as an instrument for education.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Higher educational attainment significantly reduces the risk of chronic diseases.
